In hard real-time multiprocessor systems, it is necessary to have a fault-tolerant task execution scheme to meet the tasks' deadlines even in the presence of a processorfailure. In this papel; we propose a delayed scheduling algorithm using a passive replica method. This scheme has relatively a small overhead for backup processes. For the purpose of high schedulability, we allow the primary copy of one task to overlap with the backup copy of another task. And, i f all processors are busy to execute a task, the schedule of an arriving task is delayed until at least one processor is available. A heuristic cost function is used to select the task to be scheduled next among the delayed tasks. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves higher schedulability compared to other conventional approaches and a single spare node scheme.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: In a hard real-time system, missing tasks' deadlines could cause a catastrophic result. Therefore, an appro- priate task scheduling method is required to guarantee the tasks to meet their deadlines. Some researches on the task scheduling in real-time multiprocessor systems have been reported [7,2].In spite of these efforts, a processor failure may cause the tasks to miss their deadlines. Hence, it is necessary to have a fault-tolerant task scheduling scheme to meet the tasks' deadlines even in the presence of processor failures. A few approaches on the fault-tolerant scheduling in a hard real-time multiprocessor system have been reported. All the reported approaches are based on the primaryhackup method [3, 6, l l , 41. In this method, primary and backup tasks for the same task are scheduled on different processors. The task that is arrived and executed in a normal state is called primary task. When a processor fails, the task to meet its deadline is called backup task. According to the [ 111, primaryhackup approaches are classified into two classes. First, the backup task is activated after the processor with the primary task fails. Fault tolerance is achieved through the time redundancy [3, 61. Second, primary and backup tasks are executed on different processors As mentioned in [ 113, tasks should have enough laxity to restart their backups in the first approach. That is, the laxity is larger than the computation time. In the second approach, the primary and the backup tasks are executed simultaneously. However, most of methods reported recently use the active replica model as a backup task. In the active replica model, the backup task is the same as the primary one. In other words, the backup copy has the same computation time as the primary one. Though overloading and deallocation techniques are used to reduce the overhead for backup task, backup task used in the active replica model has a relatively large overhead for backup by itself. And it may cause to lower the schedulability.
On the other hand, there have been a little consideration on this subject using a passive replica model [I]. Tandem and Delta-4 systems use the passive replica model [S, 91.

In the passive replica model, primary task checkpoints its running status to the backup running on a different processor. When a processor fails, the role of the task running on the failed processor is taken by its backup task. The execution continues from the point where the last checkpoint was made. Bertossi and Mancini [ 13 proposed a preemptive realtime task scheduling algorithm that uses the passive replica model. However, the considered task model is periodic primaryhackup tasks.

In this paper, we propose a fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm in a real-time multiprocessor system at which aperiodic tasks arrive dynamically. Our fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm uses the passive replica model. Hence, each backup task is not active until its primary task cannot be executed further or cannot meet its deadline.

We remove the restriction of tasks given in [3, 61, which tasks should have enough laxity to restart their backups. And, the delayed scheduling algorithm (DSA) proposed by us postpones the schedulability test of arrived task until there is at least one available processor. Among the tasks waiting for scheduling, the algorithm uses a heuristic cost function to select a task to be scheduled next. We compare the performance of our algorithm to those of other reported methods using active replica model, that of single spare node scheme, and those of non-fault-tolerant schemes. The simulation results show that our algorithm achieves the schedulability as high as that of non-fault-tolerant schemes. And by properly combining the weight factors of the cost function, the schedulability can be improved even more. This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we describe the previous works related to the fault-tolerant scheduling problem. In Section 3 we propose our scheduling algorithm and analyze the performance of our algorithm through the simulations in Section 4. In Section 5 we summarize and conclude the paper.

div.head: Previous Works
div.p: In this section, we present fault-tolerant real-time scheduling algorithms reported recently. Faults can he classified into two types: the task (process) fault and the processor fault. Liestman and Campbell [5] proposed a real-time scheduling algorithm which tolerates process faults. If a process does not meet its timing constraint due to the process fault, their method satisfies the timing constraint by cxccuting a backup process. Specially, thc backup process is the one that can produce some inaccurate result, which is acceptable, but it has less computation time than that of primary one. Here, we only present the real-time scheduling algorithms which tolerate processor failures.

Ghosh et al. [3, 61 proposed a fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm in a real-time multiprocessor system. Tasks are aperiodic and arrive at the system dynamically. The algorithm schedules tasks based on the primaryhackup approach and uses an active replica model as a backup task. For a primary task, the algorithm schedules it as early as possible. For a backup task the algorithm schedules it as late as possible. In addition, the algorithm uses two interesting techniques called the backup overloading and the backup deallocation. The backup overloading is the technique that schedules backups for multiple primary tasks on the same time period in order to make efficient utilization of available processor time. Of course, only backups of which the primary tasks are scheduled on different processors can be overloaded each other. The backup deallocation is the technique that deallocates the backup task of which the primary one completes successfully. After a backup task is deallocated, the time slot occupied by the backup task can be used to schedule other tasks. These two techniques are used to achieve high schedulability as well as to provide fault-tolerance. In [ 3 , 6 ] , however, a task must have enough laxity to execute its backup task after its primary one cannot meet its deadlines due to the processor failure. That is, it has a restriction that tasks must have laxity as much as the computation time at least.

To remove this restriction, Tsuchiya et al. 1101 proposed a technique which can be applied to tasks whose laxity is too short for repetition. In the algorithm, if a task does not have enough laxity for repetition, the primary and the backup tasks are executed in parallel. In this case the time slot for the execution o'f a backup task can be divided into two parts: the preceding part which is executed with the primary task simultaneously, and the remaining part which is executed after the primary copy was completed. They call the preceding part redundant part and the remaining part backup part. In order to make efficient utilization of processors, they applied the deallocation of backup part after its primary task was completed successfully. This is the same technique with the hack:up deallocation proposed in [ 3 , 6 ] . Tsuchiya et al. [ 11:I also proposed a technique which combines the technique proposed in [lo] with the one in [3, 61. They also divided the backup task into two parts: the redundant part and the backup part. If a task has enough laxity for repetition, it has only a backup part. And in this case the schedule (of backup follows the method proposed in [3, 61. And if a task does not have enough laxity for repetition, it has both of the redundant and the backup parts. And for a backup part, it can be overloaded with other backups or redundant parts of which their primaries are executed on different processors. But the redundant parts cannot be overloaded on each other. For a primary task, the algorithm schedules it as early as possible. For a backup task, if it is not required to schedule the redundant part, the algorithm schedules the backup task as late as possible. And, if ii. is required, for a redundant part, scheduler evaluates whether or not the redundant part can be scheduled on time interval [deadlinecomputation t i m e , completion t i m e of pi-imary tusk].

div.head: Heuristic selection methods
div.p: 1. We schedule the task so that the checkpoint chain is as long as possible unless checkpoint cycle is formed. In other words, for the primary task with multiple Pelsts, we select the processor which is already selected to schedule backup tasks of other primary tasks. The reason why we make the chain long is to increase the overlap of primary and backup tasks. For the backup task we select the processor on which other primary one is already being executed. 2. div.p: We compare the performance of the proposed algorithm to those of single spare node scheme, non-fault-tolerant scheme, and other reported approaches. The single spare node scheme is the method of having one spare node which is used to schedule all backup tasks. When one active node fails, the spare node takes over the role of the failed processor and the backup tasks of which primaries were on the failed node are activated. The single spare node scheme and the non-fault-tolerant scheme use the same scheduling mechanism. Only, the non-fault-tolerant scheme has one more processor to schedule tasks. We applied the following two scheduling methods as the method for the single spare and the non-fault-tolerant scheme.

div.head: Method 1
div.p: For each processor Pj, the scheduler tries to schedule Ti on the earliest free time. If it is impossible, the scheduler considers the forwarding of other scheduled tasks. And it selects the Drocessor which has the earliest start time. Method 2 * For each processor Pi, the scheduler tries to schedule Ti accordingto the earliest deadline first(EDF) policy. And it selects the processor for T, which has the earliest start time.

div.p: Table 1 shows the guaranteed ratio for various number of processors. Generated tasks' laxity weight follows uniform distribution between 0.1 and 2 and y is 0.8. We set the weight of the cost function to w 1 = w 2 = O,WQ = 1 (minimum laxity first policy). As shown in the Table 1, the DSA has higher guaranteed ratio than a single spare node scheme and "rdact". Moreover, it achieves the guaranteed ratio as high as non-fault-tolerant scheme.

Figure 5 shows the guaranteed ratio for different loads. The laxity weight follows uniform distribution between 0.1 and 3 and the number of processors is 5. As shown in the Figure 5, the greater the load is, the higher the rejection ratio of all schemes. However, the DSA achieves high schedulability than others for various loads.

Figure 6 shows the guaranteed ratio for different laxity weight. The number of processors is 5. With very small laxity weight, the non-fault-tolerant schemes achieve the high-Method 1 is used in [3, 61 for the non-fault-tolerant scheme to compare their performance. We also compare est guaranteed ratio. As the laxity weight increases, however, the DSA achieves schedulability as high as non-faulttolerant schemes. Except for small laxity weight, the DSA achieves almost the same performance as non-fault-tolerant schemes. This is due to the fact that there is less backup tasks running concurrently with primary tasks as the laxity weight increases.

In the above simulations, we considered the remaining time of a backup task is equal to that of its primary task at time t. However, the actual remaining time of a backup task is the time interval from the last checkpoint to the completion time of the task. In the following experiment, we include a checkpoint interval in calculating the remaining time of a backup task. The effect of including the checkpoint interval in calculating the remaining time is shown in Figure 7. In Figure 7, "dsa-inf" represents the case that the remaining time of the backup task is equal to that of the primary task. "dsa2c" and "dsa-4c" represent the cases that a task checkpoints only twice or four times, respectively, during its execution. When the laxity weight is 0.1, the number of checkpoints does not affect the schedulability. As the laxity weight increases, "dsa-inf" achieves the highest schedulability. This is because as we have more checkpoints, we have less rollback distance. And, as the laxity weight increases beyond 1, the number of checkpoint does not affect the schedulability. This is because a sufficient laxity compensates the difference in the remaining time.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: In this paper, we have proposed an efficient fault-tolerant task scheduling algorithm in a real-time multiprocessor system. Our approach is also based on the primaryhackup model, but uses the passive replica model for the backup task. We removed the restriction of a task given in [3, 61.
